module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Denominators of $\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k 2^k}$

$a(n)$ is the denominator of the sum
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$$

*References:*
- [A175386](https://oeis.org/A175386)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA175386


/--
$a(n)$ is the denominator of the sum
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.sum (Finset.Icc 1 n) fun i : ℕ =>
    -- The upper index is $2n - i - 1$, which is equivalent to
    -- $2n - (i+1)$ in $\mathbb{N}$ for $i \le n$.
    -- The lower index $i-1$ is standard subtraction in $\mathbb{N}$.
    let num : ℕ := Nat.choose (2 * n - (i + 1)) (i - 1)
    (num : ℚ) / (i : ℚ)
  ).den



@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 6 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by native_decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by native_decide


/--
We conjecture that $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{i} \binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$ is not an integer for $n > 1$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/175386.wip.lean#L304"]
theorem a_ne_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : a n ≠ 1 := by
    sorry

end OeisA175386

findings.description: The module heading at line 21 says “Denominators of ∑_{k=1}^n 1/(k 2^k)”, but the definition and theorem concern ∑_{i=1}^n binomial(2n-i-1,i-1)/i. These give different denominator sequences: at n=1 the heading's sum has denominator 2, whereas OeisA175386.a 1 = 1. The definition and theorem themselves match the source.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A175386, %N: “a(n) = denominator of Sum_{i=1..n} (1/i)*C(2n-i-1,i-1).” Its %C conjecture concerns non-integrality of this same binomial sum for n>1. Read through the official mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A175/A175386.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the module heading with “Denominators of $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{i}\binom{2n-i-1}{i-1}$”. No mathematical declaration needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The source says the rational sum is not an integer for every n>1; Lean states that its reduced denominator is not 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Rat stores a positive denominator coprime to its numerator. Consequently q.den = 1 iff there exists z : ℤ with (z : ℚ) = q. In scratch.lean, I proved that a n is the denominator of the source's reciprocal-times-binomial formula and then proved a n ≠ 1 ↔ ¬ ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℚ) = sourceSum n, including the universally quantified version with n>1.
